$comment: Federal civil pleading standard (Rule 8/12(b)(6) 'plausibility'). Every field verified live against CourtListener on 2026-08-22 (search + clusters + opinions-cited endpoints), not recalled from training data. Independently cross-checked: the Twombly/Iqbal citation, docket, cluster_id, and opinion_id values below were separately re-verified by a second live CourtListener query and matched exactly.
verification_method: mcp CourtListener connector: search (type=o, court=scotus/ca3) for existence/identity/citation, clusters for citation_count/precedential_status, opinions-cited for the citation-graph edges

authorities.name: Bell Atlantic Corp. v. Twombly
authorities.court: Supreme Court of the United States
authorities.proposition: A complaint must contain sufficient factual matter, accepted as true, to state a claim to relief that is 'plausible on its face' - retiring the earlier 'no set of facts' standard from Conley v. Gibson for antitrust conspiracy pleading under Rule 8(a)(2), read together with Rule 12(b)(6).
authorities.verification_note: CourtListener's own judges field for this cluster contains an anomalous token ('Auto') in place of a justice's name, reproduced identically from both the search index and the clusters endpoint - a genuine upstream data artifact, not guessed or corrected here.

authorities.name: Ashcroft v. Iqbal
authorities.court: Supreme Court of the United States
authorities.proposition: Twombly's plausibility standard applies to all civil actions under Rule 8, not only antitrust conspiracy claims. Articulates a two-step approach: (1) identify and disregard bare legal conclusions unsupported by factual allegations, then (2) assess whether the remaining well-pleaded factual allegations plausibly give rise to an entitlement to relief.
authorities.verification_note: CourtListener's judges field for this cluster returned an incomplete panel (omitting Roberts, Scalia, Thomas, Alito) - flagged as an upstream data gap rather than supplemented from general knowledge.

authorities.name: Fowler v. UPMC Shadyside
authorities.court: Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit
authorities.proposition: Applies Iqbal's two-step framework at the circuit level: disregard conclusory allegations, then assess whether the remaining well-pleaded facts nudge the claim from merely possible to plausible - one of the first circuit-level opinions to work through Iqbal's application in detail.
authorities.authority_weight_note: Binding within the Third Circuit only; persuasive elsewhere - see docs/OPERATING_RULES.md's authority hierarchy for how circuit-level authority weight varies by forum.

edges.verified_via: CourtListener opinions-cited endpoint - citing_opinion 9435339 -> cited_opinion 9435068 (citation-graph record id 300604170) confirmed. Labelled EXTENDS rather than FOLLOWS because Iqbal generalises Twombly's antitrust-context plausibility test to all civil pleading, rather than applying it in an identical context.
CourtListener opinions-cited endpoint - citing_opinion (Fowler) -> cited_opinion 9435339 (Iqbal) (citation-graph record id 269113458) confirmed direct citation.

what_this_is_not: Three cases, two verified edges, on the plausibility pleading standard from its Supreme Court origin through one circuit-level application. Does not survey how other circuits have applied Twombly/Iqbal, which varies and was not independently verified in this pass.
